files.text:
# JOURNAL — optimizer handover (append-only, whole run)

YOU (the optimizer) own this file. It is the running, accumulating handover across ALL iterations — accepted AND rejected — and it is NEVER reset. Each iteration you APPEND one new entry at the bottom (under the marker line); you do NOT edit or delete earlier entries. Read the whole journal before proposing, so you build on EVERY prior attempt (not just the last accepted one) and never re-test a refuted idea.

You CANNOT know your own gate result while you write — the harness scores you AFTER you stop and stamps a **RESULT** line (outcome + Δ + the tasks you measurably broke/fixed, plus the ones whose move was too small to resolve) right below your entry. So do NOT write 'what worked' as a guess. To learn what actually worked, READ the framework RESULT lines of prior entries (and LEDGER.md): an entry whose RESULT says `rejected` with `broke={...}` tells you which specific edits to drop or redesign — its diff.patch is in ./prior_iterations/<id>/.

Append your entry for THIS iteration below the marker, using this shape (INTENT only — the framework appends the RESULT):

    ## Iteration <your candidate id> — <one-line headline of what you tried>
    - Changes I made (1 line per edit; name the file/tool + cluster it targets):
    - Per change, the EXPECTED effect + why it's safe (which failing task it should fix;
      why no passing task changes behavior):
    - Building on prior RESULTS: which prior entries' broke/fixed I used, and what I
      did NOT re-try because a prior RESULT showed it regressed (cite ids):
    - Refuted hypotheses (a prior RESULT proved this is NOT the fix — never re-test):
    - High-value clusters still NOT cracked (and the guard/tool designs already tried):
    - Plateau signal (are the last few RESULTs flat/negative? if so, which LEVER to switch
      to — e.g. a NEW composite tool instead of another guard, or prompt instead of code):
    - Focus next iteration:

## Iteration cand_0001 — authored the EMPTY prompt.md from scratch + turned the template's vacuous "verify" turn into an ordered, falsifiable 3-stage checklist

**Starting point:** seed val 0.725 (29/40). `prompt.md` was **0 bytes** — the agent had no
system message at all. No prior iterations exist (LEDGER/RUNMAP empty, no rejected.jsonl), so
there is nothing refuted to avoid and the entire SAFE burden was on reading passing traces.
No environment fault: all 40 traces executed cleanly, `rollout.error is None` on all 40.

- **Changes I made** (all in `prompt.md` (new, 6 rules) and `task_template.md` (restructured)):
  1. `prompt.md` "How you are scored" — states the grader compares VALUES in `answer_position`
     including python TYPE, that blank-vs-value and Excel error strings both fail, and that
     Sheet-Level grades the whole region. Cluster: all 11 (contract knowledge gap).
  2. `prompt.md` Rule 1 — in-place `load_workbook`→assign A1→`save` as the DEFAULT with a
     copyable idiom, plus an escape clause for "generating the whole sheet" / "re-shape
     (sort/insert/delete/clear-and-repopulate)", plus the two-handle `data_only=True`-to-read /
     plain-to-write idiom. Cluster: 341-40, 535-20 (both had CORRECT requested edits and failed
     100% on `to_excel` collateral damage).
  3. `prompt.md` Rule 2 — address graded cells by literal A1 for both write and read-back; names
     the `read_excel(header=0)` off-by-one. Cluster: 48924 (whole answer shifted 1 row), 5835.
  4. `prompt.md` Rule 3 — "Python is your only oracle; nothing here recalculates, openpyxl stores
     no cached value". Formulas stay ALLOWED; literal value required only for array/CSE
     aggregates (`MEDIAN(IF(...))` etc.) and formulas whose error/blank inputs are unverified
     (`data_type == "e"` vs the text `"#N/A"`). Cluster: 33722, 42354, 53647.
  5. `prompt.md` Rule 4 — read `answer_position` first; pre-filled cells are the task's spec;
     disagreement means re-examine your interpretation; read stated bounds, don't `min()/max()`.
     Carve-outs: values-not-formatting, and does NOT apply where the instruction says
     delete/clear/replace. Cluster: 38985, 48924, 42354, 49036.
  6. `prompt.md` Rule 5 — decimals/percent decide the graded string; a caveat in the instruction
     is a trap to handle in code and PRINT, not to assert away in a comment; write only the
     named cells, none past the end; leave blank by leaving UNWRITTEN. Cluster: 49036, 11842,
     42354, 38985.
  7. `prompt.md` Rule 6 — recovery: identical re-run output means your edit did nothing; for real
     ambiguity compute both readings and pick the one reproducing the example cells. Cluster:
     51359 (3 write+verify rounds, byte-identical output each time, never noticed).
  8. `task_template.md` — replaced the flat 3-item round list with 3 ORDERED STAGES where stage 1
     (print `answer_position` + `data_type` by A1, and the cells the instruction names) is a
     precondition of stage 2 (compute + print expected values, then write), and stage 3 is a
     4-item checklist that can FAIL: type/`data_type` by literal A1; `None`/`NaN`/error/text-number
     are defects; printed values must match stage 2's computed numbers; and (Sheet-Level ONLY)
     diff the whole graded range output-vs-source and print every differing cell. Deleted the old
     "reply when you are satisfied the saved file is correct" in favour of "only once Stage 3
     printed real values and every item came out clean — an existing output file is not evidence
     of a correct one". Also relabelled `spreadsheet_content` as a pandas PREVIEW, not ground
     truth. Cluster: all 11 (the vacuous-verification root cause).

- **Expected effect + why safe.** Cluster 1 (vacuous verification) is present in 11/11 failures:
  every agent obeyed "print the values you wrote" literally and printed something that cannot
  disagree — formula text from a non-`data_only` handle (33722, 49036, 42354, 11842, 53647),
  hand-typed constants (38985), or a read-back reusing the write's own wrong offset (48924,
  5835) — then stopped confidently at 3-6 turns. Making the check falsifiable is the single
  highest-leverage edit. Cluster 2 recovers 341-40 and 535-20 outright: 341-40's 8 requested
  cells were CORRECT and all 955 wrong cells were ones it was never asked to touch; 535-20's
  column selection was right and all 257 errors were type/blank damage. 11842 is 94/96.
  Safety: every rule is additive and conditioned; the Sheet-Level diff cannot fire on the 25
  passing Cell-Level tasks; I verified the two 30-turn-cap passing tasks (56920, 56427) save a
  correct file at turn 1 and turn 5 respectively and spend turns 6-30 on byte-identical no-op
  re-saves, so added verification turns cannot starve them.

- **Building on prior RESULTS:** none exist. Instead I audited 15 PASSING traces with a
  read-only subagent and **rescoped three draft rules that it proved unsafe** — this is the
  part of the iteration most worth preserving:
  - "untouched cells must equal the original" would have BROKEN **13-1**, whose instruction says
    "delete the old ranges in the LISTS sheet" and whose winning turn clears stale rows INSIDE
    the graded range (`new_lists.iloc[2:32, 0:4] = ""`); also 379-36's gold overwrites 2
    pre-filled cells. → downgraded to a diff-and-review + an explicit delete/clear carve-out.
  - "no `None`/`NaN` in `answer_position`" would have BROKEN **56427**, whose gold leaves most of
    its 324 graded cells blank ("preserve blanks as blanks, not zeros"). → carved out. I also did
    NOT write a type-homogeneity rule, because 46646's gold is deliberately mixed (`0` as int).
  - bare "use openpyxl not pandas" would have BROKEN **48608** and **58147**, which read a
    formula-generated source column (48608's instruction says it comes from a "unique, filter
    formula"); a plain `load_workbook` returns `"=UNIQUE(FILTER(...))"` and their parsing
    silently yields "Not Found". → Rule 1 ships with the two-handle `data_only=True` idiom.

- **Refuted before shipping (do NOT re-test):** "write literal values, not formulas" is FALSE
  here. The grader RECALCULATES: passing 42198, 52807, 41589, 39515, 49801 each wrote only
  formula strings and scored 1.0, and 11842 got 94/96 formula cells right. That rule would be
  unbounded and regress 5+ passing tasks. Related fact: Cell-Level grading checks ONLY
  `answer_position`, so `to_excel` collateral damage is not an argument on Cell-Level tasks —
  preservation pays on Sheet-Level only.

- **High-value clusters still NOT cracked:** (a) the per-task SEMANTIC ambiguities — 51359
  ("total of consecutive 1's" = sum of streak lengths, or count of qualifying groups?) and 38985
  (which duplicate-pairing rule) — need the gold answer; encoding either reading would be a
  task-specific literal, so I attacked them only generically via Rule 6 (compute both readings,
  pick the one reproducing the pre-filled example). (b) There is NO formula evaluator in the
  sandbox — zero of 40 traces contain `data_only=True`, `soffice`, `libreoffice`, `pycel`,
  `formulas`, `xlwings` or `subprocess`. A real recalculation step would be the biggest remaining
  win on cluster 1, but it is a tooling change, not prose; suggesting `soffice` in the prompt
  would be a speculative edit against an unverified binary. Logged in FRAMEWORK_IMPROVEMENTS.md.

- **Plateau signal:** none — this is iteration 1 of 1 from an untouched baseline whose system
  prompt was literally empty, so the lever with by far the most headroom (authoring `prompt.md`
  at all) had never been pulled.

- **Focus next iteration (if one exists):** read the RESULT stamped below. If ACCEPTED, the next
  marginal gains are (i) whether Rule 1 moved the ~7 passing few-cell `to_excel` tasks without
  changing their graded values — check none of them regressed, and tighten the escape clause if
  one did; (ii) a worked end-to-end example in `prompt.md` for the Sheet-Level in-place +
  diff pattern; (iii) the two semantic-ambiguity tasks. If REJECTED, the diff is one batch of
  two files — bisect it: ship `task_template.md`'s 3-stage restructure ALONE first (it is the
  root cause of 11/11 and the least method-changing), and hold back `prompt.md` Rule 1, the one
  edit I classed as borderline-unbounded because it changes method on ~7 passing tasks.

> **RESULT (framework, measured):** REJECTED (champion unchanged) · val=0.800 Δ=+0.075 · fixed={33722, 38985, 42354, 48924, 51359, 53647} · broke={353-29, 46646, 48921} · unresolved={—} (moved less than 2·SE of its own measurement — NOT evidence the edit touched those tasks; do not redesign on them). — its WHOLE batch was reverted; re-introduce only the edits that did NOT break a task above, dropping/redesigning the ones that did.

files.title: Insights — verified findings
files.text:
# INSIGHTS — summarized, verified findings (accumulate across the whole run)

The JOURNAL is your per-iteration diary; THIS file is the distilled, VERIFIED takeaway a future iteration should read instead of re-reading the whole journal or old sessions/traces. Update it whenever you have a genuinely NEW, confirmed finding (an accepted/rejected RESULT counts as confirmation; a guess does not) — not every iteration needs a new entry. Structure each addition as:

    ## <task or mechanism name>
    - What worked (confirmed by a RESULT, cite the candidate id):
    - What didn't (confirmed by a RESULT, cite the candidate id):
    - Promising but not yet tried:

## The grader RECALCULATES formulas (established from traces, pre-gate)
- **What worked:** nothing to cite yet (iteration 1). But this is a measured FACT from the seed's
  own scored traces, not a guess: passing tasks 42198, 52807, 41589, 39515, 49801 each wrote ONLY
  Excel formula strings via openpyxl, never computed a value, and scored 1.0; 11842 wrote 96
  formulas and 94 recalculated to the expected value.
- **What didn't:** a blanket "write literal values, not formulas" rule is therefore FALSE and
  UNBOUNDED — it would flip 5+ passing tasks. Never propose it.
- **The narrow true version:** openpyxl cannot write an ARRAY/CSE formula. `MEDIAN(IF(...))`,
  `SUM(IF(...))`, `MAX(IF(...))` are stored as scalar formulas, the inner condition collapses to
  the range's first cell, and the cell recalculates to a plausible WRONG number (33722: "5 of 5
  cells differ, different value of the right type"). Only that subclass needs a literal value.

## Cell-Level grades ONLY answer_position; Sheet-Level grades the whole region
- Feedback phrase "CHANGED although the expected value is the cell's own original input" appears
  in 5 of 11 failures and in 0 of 29 passing ones. On Sheet-Level it is fatal: 341-40's 8
  requested cells were CORRECT and it scored 0 because a `pd.read_excel`→`to_excel` round trip
  altered 955 cells it was never asked to touch (700 of them "the CORRECT value stored as text
  instead of as a number/date"). 535-20 likewise: column selection right, 257 cells of type/blank
  damage.
- So argue in-place editing from FIDELITY on Cell-Level tasks and from GRADING on Sheet-Level.
  11 passing tasks use `pandas.to_excel` — a blanket ban is unsafe.

## There is no formula evaluator in the sandbox
- Across all 40 traces, zero occurrences of `data_only=True`, `soffice`, `libreoffice`, `pycel`,
  `formulas`, `xlwings`, `subprocess`. Nothing recalculates, and openpyxl writes formulas with no
  cached value — so the agent literally cannot observe what the grader will read from a formula
  cell. This is why the seed's "verification" turn was vacuous in 11/11 failures.
- **Promising but not yet tried:** giving the agent a real recalculation path (headless
  LibreOffice, or the `formulas`/`pycel` packages) would attack the largest cluster at its root.
  It is a TOOLING change, not prose — do not fake it with a prompt line telling the agent to
  shell out to an unverified binary.

## Three prompt rules that LOOK safe and are not (checked against passing traces)
- "Untouched cells in the graded range must equal the original" breaks **13-1**: its instruction
  says to delete the old ranges, and the winning turn clears stale rows INSIDE the graded range.
  379-36's gold also overwrites pre-filled cells. Any preservation rule needs a delete/clear
  carve-out.
- "No `None`/`NaN` in `answer_position`" breaks **56427**: its gold leaves most of 324 graded
  cells blank ("preserve blanks as blanks, not zeros"). Blank can be the right answer.
- "Prefer openpyxl over pandas" breaks **48608** and **58147** unless paired with
  `data_only=True`: their source columns are formula-generated, so a plain `load_workbook`
  returns formula TEXT and their parsing silently degrades to a wrong-but-plausible answer.
- Also: do NOT require type homogeneity across the graded range — **46646**'s gold is
  deliberately mixed (`0` as int, the rest float) because its instruction says a zero value has
  no decimal places.

files.title: Meta-insights — the optimization process
files.text:
# META-INSIGHTS — about the optimization PROCESS itself (this run)

Not about the capability — about HOW this run is searching for it: which strategies/edit classes/algorithms are helping vs stalling, and what to try next iteration. Update at the end of the run at minimum; sooner if a plateau or a clear strategy shift is worth recording now. Structure each addition as:

    ## Iteration <id> (or 'run so far')
    - Strategy tried, and whether it moved val (cite LEDGER rows):
    - Plateau/stall signal, if any, and the lever switched to:
    - What to try next iteration:

## Iteration cand_0001 (the run's only iteration)
- **Strategy tried:** breadth-first. Diagnose all 11 failures at once with 2 parallel read-only
  subagents, cluster by shared root cause (8 clusters found), then ship one fix per cluster in a
  single candidate across both editable files. Cannot cite a LEDGER row — the LEDGER was empty at
  the start and the RESULT for this candidate is stamped after I stop.
- **The highest-value thing I did was NOT diagnosis — it was checking my rules against the
  PASSING traces before shipping.** A third read-only subagent audited 15 passing traces against
  3 draft rules and proved all 3 would regress a passing task (13-1, 56427, 48608/58147). Each
  survived only because I added a carve-out. With a 1-iteration budget and a gate that rejects
  net-zero, an unchecked plausible rule is the main way to lose the whole candidate. **Budget
  roughly as much effort on the passing traces as on the failing ones.**
- **The second-highest-value thing was falsifying the obvious fix.** The 11 failures scream
  "formulas don't evaluate → write values instead". Five PASSING tasks wrote formula-only output
  and scored 1.0, so that rule would have been unbounded and wrong. A 10-minute census over all
  40 traces (method used × reward) caught it. **Always cross-tabulate the proposed rule's variable
  against reward over ALL tasks, not just the failing ones.**
- **Look for the empty file.** `prompt.md` was 0 bytes: ~40% of the agent's stated instruction
  surface was unused, and no amount of wordsmithing the template would have substituted. Check
  artifact SIZES first — an empty or stub capability file is the cheapest large win available.
- **Diagnostic tell worth reusing:** turn count vs. reward. Every failure stopped at 3-6 turns;
  several passing tasks used 7-30. The seed's verification step consumed a turn and returned zero
  bits, which manufactured false confidence. When a "verify" step cannot disagree with the work it
  checks, it is worse than no step — it licenses stopping.
- **Plateau/stall signal:** none to report (single iteration from an untouched baseline).
- **What to try next iteration:** read the RESULT first. If ACCEPTED, the remaining headroom is
  the 2 semantic-ambiguity tasks (51359, 38985) and a worked end-to-end Sheet-Level example;
  also confirm the ~7 passing few-cell `to_excel` tasks were not disturbed by Rule 1. If
  REJECTED, **bisect rather than abandon** — ship `task_template.md`'s 3-stage restructure alone
  (root cause of 11/11, least method-changing) and hold back `prompt.md` Rule 1, the only edit
  classed borderline-unbounded. A 2-file batch is near the limit of what one gate result can
  attribute; with a longer budget I would have split method-changing edits from
  contract-clarifying ones into separate candidates.

files.name: FRAMEWORK_IMPROVEMENTS.md
files.title: Framework improvements — for cap-evolve itself
files.text:
# FRAMEWORK-IMPROVEMENTS — suggestions for cap-evolve itself (cross-run)

NOT about this capability or this run's result — about what cap-evolve the FRAMEWORK should change so FUTURE runs (any capability, any project) go better: a confusing prompt section, a missing tool, a file you wished existed, a gate that felt wrong. Optional most iterations; add an entry whenever something about the framework itself (not the task) got in your way or surprised you.

## From iteration cand_0001 (spreadsheetbench, system-prompt capability)

1. **Surface the passing traces as first-class input, not just a list of ids to protect.**
   INSTRUCTIONS.md gives full feedback for the 11 failures and only bare ids for the 29 passing
   tasks — but the SAFE test is entirely about the passing ones, and three of my draft rules were
   provably regression-causing only because I went and read those traces myself. A "## Passing
   tasks, grouped by the method/decision they relied on" block, or even just a note that the
   passing traces are in the same directory and should be audited, would make the most
   regression-prone step the obvious one instead of the optional one.

2. **Tell the optimizer which artifact files are EMPTY or stub.** The single largest lever here
   was that `prompt.md` was 0 bytes. INSTRUCTIONS.md described it as "~40% of the words the agent
   reads", which is actively misleading when the file is empty — an optimizer that trusted that
   line would have gone looking for wording to sharpen and found nothing. Report each editable
   artifact's size/line count in the edit-space section.

3. **The benchmark's own contract facts belong in the instructions, not in the traces.** Two facts
   decided most of my edits and both had to be reverse-engineered from scored rollouts: (a) the
   scorer RECALCULATES formulas before comparing, and (b) Cell-Level compares only
   `answer_position` while Sheet-Level compares the whole region. These are properties of the
   harness, not of any task, so stating them would not leak gold — and getting (a) wrong would
   have produced a confidently-stated false contract in the prompt, exactly the failure mode
   INSTRUCTIONS.md warns about. Consider a short "what the scorer does" section for the project.

4. **A 1-iteration budget conflicts with the "ship as many fixes as you can" directive.** The
   instructions push hard for breadth, while the gate returns one accept/reject over the whole
   batch — so a 9-edit candidate that regresses one passing task teaches almost nothing about the
   other 8. With `iteration 1/1` the incentive is right (breadth is the only shot), but the
   framework could help attribution by scoring 2-3 sub-batches when the budget allows, or by
   letting the optimizer TAG edits so the RESULT can be attributed per tag.

5. **`{max_turns}` being optional is a trap worth flagging.** The template's turn budget interacts
   directly with any edit that adds verification steps. I had to check by hand whether the two
   passing tasks that hit the 30-turn cap would be starved of a save (they would not — both saved
   early and then looped on identical no-op re-saves). A per-task "turns used / cap" column in the
   failing+passing summary would make that check cheap. Relatedly: degenerate identical-re-save
   loops burned ~25 turns on 2 passing tasks, which looks like something the adapter could detect
   and stop.

6. **Minor:** INSTRUCTIONS.md interpolates the whole edit-space block inline twice (in "WHAT YOU
   MAY EDIT" and again in "Self-check"), including the nested bullet list and the `SKILL.md`
   path, which makes the surrounding sentence hard to parse on first read. A reference to the
   section would read better than a second full inlining.

# Optimize the capability — ship several REAL, SAFE, VERIFIED prompt fixes this iteration

{{TARGET_READER}}

{{FOCUS_SUMMARY}}

{{EMPTY_SEED}}

GOAL: raise the eval score as much as you can THIS iteration, then STOP (the harness
re-scores you — don't run evaluation yourself). The capability under optimization is
PROSE: the agent's prompt / skill text. There are no tool implementations to edit here.

Make **AS MANY real fixes as you can this iteration — solve many issues across many
trajectories, not just the biggest one.** A timid one- or two-edit iteration is an
under-used iteration: diagnose EVERY failure cluster in `./trajectories/` and ship a fix
for each one that passes the three tests below. Breadth is the goal — the more distinct
failing clusters you fix in this ONE candidate, the larger the gain.

The ONLY brake on breadth is regression: every edit must pass all three tests, because a
single speculative edit that breaks a passing task can sink an iteration of good work (it
did in prior runs). So the discipline is "many fixes, each one real and safe" — NOT "few
fixes". Do not stop at the first cluster; work through them all.

## WHAT YOU MAY EDIT — and the two ways iterations get wasted here
Edit ONLY the capability files listed in `{{CAP_BRIEF}}` below (the prompt / skill text in
this working directory). Everything else you can see is READ-ONLY CONTEXT.

**You may NOT edit the adapter, the harness, the scorer, the benchmark, or the
environment** — not to make a task pass, not to fix a broken mount or a missing binary,
not "just to unblock the run". Those files are how your score is MEASURED; changing them
does not improve the capability, and a gain obtained that way is not a result. An
iteration that edits infrastructure has produced NOTHING measurable, however green the
number looks. **If the traces show an ENVIRONMENT fault** (permission denied, missing
binary, gateway/network error, timeout, container failure — the same error on nearly every
task, unrelated to the task's content), then the correct and complete action is:
1. do NOT edit the prompt to work around it (a prose workaround for a broken environment
   is a speculative edit that fails the REAL test — the prompt is not the defect), and
2. state the diagnosis in `PROCESS.md` and `JOURNAL.md` precisely — the exact error, how
   many tasks it hit, and what a human must fix — then STOP. Handing back an accurate
   "the environment is broken, here is the evidence" is a SUCCESSFUL iteration.

**The other way iterations get wasted: another prose rule for a behavior the agent already
knows.** When the agent has the rule and skips it anyway, adding a second sentence saying
the same thing changes nothing — you must change the STRUCTURE that makes it skippable
(see the levers below): make the step unavoidable and ordered, make the contract explicit,
or give a worked example it can pattern-match. Prose is for genuine KNOWLEDGE gaps (a
fact / format / criterion the agent cannot derive) and for STRUCTURE that changes what the
agent does — not for repetition or emphasis.

Before you keep any edit, confirm all three. Drop any edit that fails even one.
1. **REAL** — it targets a cluster that is FAILING in THIS iteration's `./trajectories/`

2. **SAFE (bounded blast radius)** — the real regression question is *behavioral*:
   **would this edit change what the agent DOES on ANY currently-passing task?** Two

   - **BOUNDED** — an ADDITIVE rule that applies only under a stated condition present in
